full_judgment:
4. The learned Subordinate Judge by his impugned judgment dated 10-7-65 was pleased to decree the suit in the preliminary form. Thereafter opposite party No 1, who was defendant No. 7 in the suit, filed on 20-7-67 an application praying for appointment of an Advocate Commissioner for effecting partition of the suit property in terms of the preliminary decree and the learned Subordinate Judge by his order dated 16-8-67 was pleased to allow the said prayer and directed the decree holder to deposit the requisite commission fees. The learned Subordinate Judge was eventually pleased to accept the Advocate Commissioner''s Report on 3-5-84, although the judgment-debors raised objection against the said report. The preliminary decree was subsequently made final on 3-5-84. 

 5. On 6-8-1986 the petitioners filed an application for staying all further proceeding of Execution Case No. 67 of 1985 alleging, inter alia, that the predecessor-in-interest defendant No. 5 Abdus Salam had died on 3-3-84 ie about two months before passing of the final decree on 3-5-1984 and, as such, the said final decree is a nullity in the eye of law and consequently the petitioners prayed for setting aside the final decree as being passed against a dead man in defendant No. 5 Abdus Salam and prayed for staying all further proceeding of the Execution Case in question. The learned Subordinate Judge by the impugned order dated 13-8-86 rejected the petitioners'' prayer holding that although defendant No. 5 died on 3-3-84 and the final decree was passed on 3-5-84 the decree in question cannot be treated as a nullity in view of the provision of Order 22 rule 4(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 7. There is no dispute to the fact that deceased defendant No. 5 Abdus Salam filed written statement in the suit and contested the suit by adducing evidence and he was allotted a saham for 1.31 acre of land. There is also no dispute to the fact that deceased defendant No. 5 Abdus Salam, one of the judgment-debtors, died on 3-3-84 before the passing of the final decree on 3-5-84. It is thus manifestly evident that the final decree was passed against deceased defendant No. 5 Abdus Salam without bringing his legal representatives on record by way of necessary substitution. It is true, the rights of the contending parties in a suit for partition are determined in the preliminary decree and the final decree is just a follow-up of the preliminary decree in effecting partition of the suit properties by metes and bounds keeping in view the existing possession of the parties as far as practicable. The final decree is, in fact, a continuation of the preliminary decree in course of which the parties are put to actual physical possession of the suit properties according to sahams allotted to them. So, if the final decree is completed in the absence of a party who was allotted a specific saham it is likely that his vital interest go unrepresented and he is adversely affected thereby. Since, in the instant case, a definite saham measaring 1.31 acre of land was allotted to deceased-defendant No. 5 Abdus Salam he had and after his death, his legal representatives have a right to get possession in their allotted saham with reference to the existing possession of the parties but unless they were brought on record their interests can be said to be properly safeguarded by the action of the Advocate-Commissioner, against whose report written objection had already been filed. Since evidently the final decree was passed against deceased defendant No. 5 Abdus Salam on 3-5-84 ie after two month of his death without bringing his legal representatives on record by way of substitution, it is to be held that vital interests of the petitioners have been adversely affected in effecting the final decree in their absence.
